safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 2.0 days to 0.43 days — current setting is overly conservative given observed supplier performance

narrative: Material PL1__M665CA02 exhibits an erratic but predominantly positive daily demand pattern (CV=0.21) across 70 working days, with a mean of ~2,887 units/day. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.23, mean 1.14 days), warranting a safety stock of 1,599 units to meet the 95% service level. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: the large EOQ of ~83,628 is capped to 24,308 by the storage capacity constraint, reducing annual orders from 108 to 29 and cutting total costs by 53%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous with high non-zero fraction (98.6%) and moderate CV (0.21), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The EOQ formula minimizes ordering vs. holding cost tradeoff; MOQ of 6,594 is non-binding since EOQ exceeds it. Storage capacity is the binding constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap reduces order quantity from EOQ of ~83,628 to 24,308 units, increasing ordering frequency from the unconstrained optimum. This raises annual ordering costs but remains significantly better than the SAP baseline of 108 orders/year. Service level is preserved via the safety stock of 1,599 units.
